q: A railway servant appointed in 1998 has emoluments of Rs 50,000 per month and is subscribing Rs 2,000 per month to SRPF. The Accounts Office objects to the subscription. What is the correct position?

options.A: The subscription is in order because any amount in whole rupees is permitted
options.B: The subscription is below the minimum of 6% of emoluments, i.e. Rs 3,000, and must be raised to at least that amount
options.C: The subscription must be exactly 10% of emoluments on the NPS pattern
options.D: The subscription should be stopped because Government makes no contribution

q: A subscriber with 8 years of service applies for a temporary advance from SRPF to finance a pleasure trip abroad for his family. How should the application be dealt with?

options.A: Sanction it within the limit of three months' pay or half the balance, whichever is less
options.B: Sanction it as a final withdrawal because 8 years of service is sufficient
options.C: Reject it because a pleasure trip is not a permissible purpose for a PF temporary advance
options.D: Sanction it with interest charged at the Government-notified rate

q: A subscriber is due to retire on superannuation in 8 months. He applies to withdraw from SRPF without assigning any reason. What is the maximum he can withdraw?

options.A: Up to 75% of the balance at credit, as in an ordinary final withdrawal
options.B: Up to 50% of the balance at credit only
options.C: The entire balance at credit, because retirement is near
options.D: Up to 90% of the balance at credit, within 12 months before retirement, without assigning any reason

Consider the following statements about interest on SRPF/GPF:
